articles.title: How Celtic's Champions League capitulation unfolded
articles.summary: BBC Scotland guides you through the timeline in Celtic's Champions League reverse in Austria.
articles.body:
All applicable, all too familiar, all can be levied at Celtic after their Champions League qualification blunder away to LASK .

A night that started full of hope and optimism as Celtic edged four goals clear on aggregate after 21 minutes ended in deep humiliation in a 5-4 aggregate defeat after extra time.

At the same stage last season, their disastrous loss to Kairat Almaty ultimately cast a long shadow over their season and was the nexus point for an overflow of negative fan sentiment towards the club.

Here's how Celtic's nightmare evening unfolded.

23' LASK 0-1 Celtic (agg 0-4) - McGregor

LASK started strongly but nowhere near as well as they finished it.

A few chances passed them by before Yang Hyun-jun showed great poise wide on the left to drive forward, cut inside, and pull it back for captain Callum McGregor to step on to.

His strike was deflected past a helpless goalkeeper and gave his side a 4-0 aggregate lead after 21 minutes.

"We're having a party in the Champions League" was the chant coming from the pocket of Celtic fans over on the far side.

Their passage to the Champions League seemed nigh on inevitable.

Samuel Adeniran nodded off target just after the restart and then pulled one wide - the warning signs were there.

LASK had passed up a glut of chances but didn't need to work hard to draw level on the night.

Moses Usor pounced on Benjamin Nygren's pass straight into his path and coolly finished to spark a little bit of hope inside the Raiffeisen Arena.

Surely Celtic had banished their Kairat demons? Surely this would be scant consolation for the hosts?

"It's a lovely composed finish, but that is an absolute gift," James McFadden said on BBC Radio Scotland.

An uneventful opening few minutes to the second half came and went without note.

Then Robert Ljubicic gave the home fans an almighty dose of confidence.

Defender Auston Trusty was caught lacking, and Ljubicic was afforded far too much time to shape and shoot on the edge of the area.

Viljami Sinisalo was beaten low to his left, and Celtic were utterly stunned.

"That is unacceptable," McFadden said on BBC Radio Scotland when describing Trusty's defending.

Major cracks were exposed in Celtic's ability to deal with LASK's rampant press and front-foot football.

LASK took the lead on the night. 48 minutes, 2-1.

LASK pulled further into the lead on the night and were only one goal back on aggregate thanks to a sensational Adeniran strike.

Alarm bells were blaring for the visitors.

Sascha Horvath did ever so well to advance the ball, lift his head, and roll it into his team-mate's path, who stepped on to the ball and curled it in from 25 yards with a sumptuous first-time effort.

Celtic had no response. The hosts were the only side looking likely to score.

The team were flat-footed and bereft of all confidence; from this point on, the game was played almost exclusively in their half.

For all of LASK's huffing and puffing, they were unable to find the all-important leveller in the tie.

The bar was struck, crosses whizzed across the goal, and chance after chance was spurned.

The home side chucked everything they had at Celtic. Corners were whipped in, headers glanced wide, and through balls drilled into the area.

They couldn't get it over the line, though. That one final bounce of the ball didn't drop in their favour.

Sinisalo pulled off a terrific stop to slap Alemao's close-range header away, but no-one had picked up Florian Flecker, who nodded in the equaliser as the time ticked into the four added minutes shown by the fourth official.

McFadden said: "Credit LASK because they haven't given in, but Celtic have created problems for themselves."

Celtic had come so close to the Champions League proper, they were now clinging on.

Often, extra time is a damp squib these days, particularly in big games.

Neither side wants to lose, and both will be happy to take a chance on penalties.

With 11 minutes still to play, Luke McCowan won the ball back for his side, but he was far too pedestrian in his decision-making, and he was dispossessed.

Another Adeniran goal from outside the box punished Celtic yet again.

The Champions League now felt like a distant dream, in stark contrast to the tangible next step of earlier on.

Sinisalo got down to make a huge save to deny Adeniran a hat-trick from the spot, but a few minutes later it meant nothing.

120 minutes. 5-4 on aggregate. Celtic's humiliation complete.

"It looked to me as if Celtic were exhausted," former Celtic manager Neil Lennon told Amazon Prime. "Fragile in duels. It only looked like there would be one winner.

"Huge credit to LASK. They battered Celtic tonight, physically and on the football side. It could have been more."

articles.title: FECIEPAR-PA Santarém: inscrições para feira terminam nesta segunda | G1
articles.standfirst: Alunos do ensino fundamental da rede municipal podem submeter projetos de sustentabilidade online. Evento presencial ocorre em setembro com exposição de trabalhos.
articles.summary: A FECIEPAR-PA Santarém encerra inscrições para projetos de sustentabilidade de alunos do ensino fundamental nesta segunda-feira, com submissão online gratuita pela plataforma Even3.
articles.body:
Escola do Parque em Santarém — Foto: Agência Santarém/Divulgação

Estudantes e professores da rede municipal de Santarém, no oeste do Pará, têm até o dia 31 de agosto de 2026 para se inscrever gratuitamente na I Feira Municipal Eco Científica da Escola do Parque (FECIEPAR-PA). Promovido pela Secretaria Municipal de Educação (Semed), o evento busca transformar a curiosidade dos alunos em pesquisa científica focada na sustentabilidade amazônica.

A participação é voltada para turmas do 1º ao 9º ano do ensino fundamental vinculadas ao Projeto Liga Estudantil do Meio Ambiente (Lema). O processo é totalmente digital, e os interessados devem enviar os resumos dos trabalhos por meio da plataforma Even3 . Cada equipe pode ter até três estudantes, sempre com a orientação direta de um professor.

As pesquisas submetidas precisam apresentar soluções para desafios socioambientais da região. Para organizar as apresentações, o edital dividiu os projetos em eixos temáticos que incluem conservação da biodiversidade, agroecologia, mudanças climáticas, saúde ambiental, além de tecnologias e saberes tradicionais.

A feira ocorrerá de forma presencial no dia 25 de setembro de 2026, na Escola Municipal de Educação Ambiental – Escola do Parque. A programação começará às 7h30 com o credenciamento e a abertura oficial, seguida pela exposição dos projetos em estandes, das 8h às 12h. Os trabalhos de maior destaque representarão o município na 9ª FECITBA-PA e na 4ª FECITBA-PA Júnior.

articles.title: Irish League: What is the relationship between gambling and football in Northern Ireland?
articles.summary: From changing culture to investment and criticism, BBC Sport NI examines the Irish League's ever-changing relationship with gambling.
articles.body:
Looking back at his 20-year career in the Irish League, Aaron Hogg remembers the first time he went to the bookies with his team-mates.

A teenager at the time, he did not know the journey it would set him upon. It was a road of debt, broken relationships and severe depression.

The goalkeeper was not the first Irish League player to have a gambling addiction, and he will not be the last.

But now, eight years since he last placed a bet, he is at the heart of an initiative to try and help those who need it through the new player-led Gambling Support Group (GSG).

Its introduction coincides with increased sponsorship of the men's and women's Irish Premiership from betting companies from this season, while the two League Cups and a regional tournament are also sponsored by bookmakers.

From culture to investment and criticism, BBC Sport NI examines the Irish League's relationship with gambling.

How Premier League shirts will change with gambling sponsor ban

When Hogg started gambling it was for fun, with fruit machines and playing pool as a teenager.

When he stepped into men's football with Crusaders, he would start to go to the bookies with team-mates before matches.

Then he was introduced to horse racing and roulette. Things spiralled from there.

"Gambling's a progressive illness," he said.

"You don't just start off by doing a bet and then all of a sudden you lose your house."

Ultimately, playing football became his "release".

"It was brilliant because my head was completely concentrated on that game and everything else went away, I was at peace for 90 minutes.

"But then I walked back into the dressing room, and as soon as you sit back down your world comes back down on top of you.

"As a gambler, you don't deal with any of your problems. You shy away from everybody, and you try and get more and more money to gamble and dig yourself deeper and deeper in the hole."

The Irish FA's betting regulations in Northern Ireland say that players cannot bet on any matches involving their team - at men's, women's or underage level - or league, and no one can place a bet on their behalf.

Michael Carvill, head of the Professional Footballers' Association in Northern Ireland, said it was something he had noticed in a 15-year career at the top of the Irish League.

The PFA are working with the Irish FA and former players with the Gambling Support Group, where support and education are key.

Carvill relates to his former Crusaders team-mate Matthew Snoddy, who is one of four players involved in the GSG alongside Hogg, Aaron Traynor and Michael Ruddy.

"I sat beside Matthew for seven years and I never knew he had an issue," said Carvill, who added you could see players' moods change whenever they checked their phones immediately after games.

"It's something that is concerning when you think you can share a changing room, train with them three nights a week and play with them and you're not aware of what's going on.

"It's really a wake-up call for all of us that this isn't going away. We have to set up something to try and treat it, and that's the purpose of this project."

As Carvill points out, gambling goes far beyond the traditional forms of betting - something he says has "increased risk".

He touches on prize websites and competitions on TV, and says it is even being found in the academy levels of the game in Northern Ireland through gaming and in-game purchases.

Across his career in the Irish League, which started in 2006, Hogg witnessed first hand how the gambling industry changed, and how that impacted players.

While you used to have to go into the bookies to physically place a bet, with smartphones you can now gamble 24/7, and on endless things.

"The markets are now more advanced. It's now become, like roulette, it's almost instant," he said.

"Betting habits have changed. Back then, when I started, there was more a social aspect to it.

"There's just so much accessibility now that it is becoming more and more prevalent to footballers."

From the start of this season, betting sponsorship is banned on the front of shirts in England in the Premier League, but still allowed on sleeves and training kits.

The ban, which was voluntarily voted for by clubs, meant eight sides had to find new front of sh i rt sponsors for the upcoming season.

Things are different in the Championship in England, where there are not the same restrictions, and in Scotland, where the SPL is sponsored by a betting company and both champions Celtic and rivals Rangers currently have betting companies on the front of their shirts.

In the Irish Premiership, three clubs - Glentoran, Cliftonville and Crusaders - are all sponsored by betting companies on the front of their shirts, while Linfield have one on their sleeve and champions Larne have it on the backs of their shirts.

Crusaders carry their betting sponsor in the Women's Premiership, while Glentoran's Oval ground in east Belfast also carries the name of a betting company.

The league's new sponsorship deal with a bookmakers also means that the betting company will be on the sleeves of players, on sponsor boards and player of the match trophies, and on the league's social media branding.

One match, over 5,000 gambling ads - is 'ban' really working?

Hooked on risk - gambling's grip on elite sport

Tommy Canning is in a unique position. He has coached in both the Irish League and in the League of Ireland, and also in both the men's and women's games.

His day job is as head of treatment at Northlands Addiction Clinic, which deals with issues involving alcohol, drugs and gambling.

When the deal for Boyle Sports to sponsor the Irish Premiership was announced, NIFL says the deal was "the league's first partnership valued at more than £1m".

Canning is critical of the move to have increased gambling sponsorship within the league, and says "what's the cost?" at the expense of increased investment.

He questioned if there were "no other avenues" available to being investment into the league.

"I'm not naive and I understand that without the right sponsorship, nothing can really develop their product.

"But it's disappointing that somewhere in the midst of this, that the integrity doesn't take over from the investment in the product.

"In terms of these sponsorship deals, they are highly lucrative and that can make it difficult for organisations to turn them down.

"But the question that I have asked in the past, and I would ask again, is at what cost are you happy to accept these lucrative deals?

"I think football clubs have a huge role socially and at a community level within the island of Ireland, and they have a responsibility to maintain some levels of integrity in terms of this issue."

Canning said, when you "understand the power of advertising", that it was "irresponsible of organisations like NIFL to be going down this road".

He added it was a "huge concern", and points to how the advertisement of tobacco and alcohol have been banned in sport, and says something similar should happen with gambling.

"There's a direct correlation between advertising and sales, and gambling is the same," he said.

"Although you're not buying anything in terms of physical thing, the impact or the correlation between the advertising of it and somebody then beginning to buy that product are very substantial in terms of the money that's spent.

"Now, not everyone is going to get into trouble, but if more people are doing it and it's more accessible, then the equation of that is that more people are going to get into trouble."

NIFL said, as part of the deal, that Boyle Sports "will launch a responsible gambling awareness initiative across NIFL clubs, using the league's matchday and digital platforms to promote practical information, encourage safer betting conversations and support fans throughout the season".

"I think there's a huge amount of hypocrisy in that statement that 'we're going to take money from betting companies, but you know what? We're going to help you more when you get into trouble'," Canning added.

"I think that's a crazy statement to make, and that's a wee bit about trying to soften the acceptance of the sponsorship. I think that there's huge hypocrisy in it."

The Northern Ireland Football League declined to comment when contacted by BBC Sport.

The Gambling Support Group is the first support group in relation to that form of addiction in the Irish League.

The fact you only have to send a text or scan a QR code, rather than pick up the phone, is a small yet important detail, and information on how to get in touch have been made available in every ground in the Irish Premiership.

"When I was gambling, I was very alone.. I pushed away my wife, my kids," continued Hogg.

"My mum and dad didn't speak to me for a couple of years. You destroy relationships and gambling destroys families.

"Sitting in the house on your own when you've lost everything, and it's just you and your own thoughts - which can be really deep, dark thoughts and depressed - the last thing you want to do is pick the phone up and speak to somebody.

"But to just pick up and text is less personal, and nobody else will have to know."

Hogg said that he can relate to any players who are struggling, and says there "will be no judgement or no shock factor".

"I'll understand everything they're talking about and I can relate to that.

"I haven't had a bet in eight years and my life has turned around full circle. I've got my relationships back, I feel good and I can offer help.

"There is hope and there is life for anybody out there that is struggling with gambling. It doesn't have to be your life."

Carvill added that the GSG is about support, not punishment, which he feels does not tackle the issue and can sometimes make things worse for those affected.

"The good thing about the PFA, which is probably different than the Irish FA, we're not the police, so to speak.

"We're not going to sanction you or punish you or tell you what you're doing is wrong. That's not our role.

"Our role is you can speak to us. It stays with us and we have to get you help."

While the vast majority of gambling issues are in men, women are not immune from addiction issues.

While the four players involved in the GSG played in the men's game, Carvill says that building relationships is key in the Women's Premiership.

"If you don't have a relationship, they're not going to speak to you. You have to connect with them before you can correct them, as I always say.

"Just because it hasn't been promoted as much, in terms of what's been shared about issues, it doesn't mean it's not happening in the women's game."

Carvill said that "one of the most concerning things" is that there is not a gambling commission in Northern Ireland, which limits regulation and the influence that can be had at government level.

For the PFA and GSG, it is about making an impact where they can.

"We are hoping to help, that's our responsibility. Ours is not to change the landscape.

"Ours is to help support the players that are in crisis and obviously prevent the next batch of young players stepping into that dressing room."

The GSG is initially being launched as a one-year scheme with QR codes and posters dotted throughout grounds, but Carvill and Hogg both hope it turns into something more long term.

Hogg says he is "not cured and not fixed" and, while he admits he will have a gambling addiction for the rest of my life, he now has the tools to help him with his recovery.

"In this world, you're never going to escape gambling, whether it be at football, whether it be at work, whether it be at driving," he said.

Even the biggest critics of gambling in football are not naive enough to know it will simply disappear, and that is why Carvill wants the GSG to become an expanded resource.

"If we're coming out and saying there's an issue and there's a problem, but we're not providing a service to support our members, then we're doing a disservice to footballers in Northern Ireland," Carvill said.

"It would be great if we didn't need it, but the reality is we are going to need it.

"It's up to us to make sure we have it in place so that moving forward, we can continue to educate and help players that are struggling."

If you have been affected by issues raised in this article, there is information and support available on BBC Action Line.

articles.title: 'No major damage' for Forfar player after game abandoned for neck injury
articles.summary: Forfar Athletic say Adam Livingstone has not suffered any major damage after  Tuesday's Challenge Cup match against Formartine United was abandoned because of a neck injury suffered by the defender.
articles.body:
Forfar Athletic say Adam Livingstone has not suffered any major damage after Tuesday's Challenge Cup match against Formartine United was abandoned because of a neck injury suffered by the defender.

Forfar led 1-0 when Livingstone was hurt in an aerial clash early in the second half.

He received treatment on the pitch and was subsequently taken to Ninewells Hospital in Dundee, where he stayed overnight.

"Following last night's injury, Adam was taken to Ninewells Hospital where X-ray results have not shown any major damage," Forfar said in a statement on Wednesday.

"Adam was kept in hospital overnight but we have been advised that, all being well, he should be allowed home later today."

articles.title: Emi Martinez transfer news: Chelsea in contact over move for Aston Villa goalkeeper
articles.summary: Chelsea consider a move for Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez after making contact with the Argentina international's representatives.
articles.body:
Chelsea are considering a move for Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez after making contact with the Argentina international's representatives.

The 33-year-old is considered available for a potential transfer from Villa after the club signed Japan goalkeeper Zion Suzuki from Parma for about £30m earlier this month.

The move could provide another opportunity for Chelsea and Villa to do business. Chelsea signed forward Morgan Rogers from Villa for a club-record £117m, while Alejandro Garnacho moved in the opposite direction on an initial loan deal.

Striker Nicolas Jackson, valued around £65m, could also join Villa and be reunited with his former manager, Unai Emery.

The clubs are known to have a close relationship. They were also involved in a deal widely described as a "PSR swap", which saw defender Ian Maatsen join Villa and Omari Kellyman, who is now at Strasbourg, move to Chelsea .

Juventus attempted to sign Martinez earlier in the transfer window, but the deal collapsed because of concerns over a finger injury.

The Italian club instead signed Tottenham goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario on loan.

The potential move comes amid concerns over the performances of Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sanchez.

Sanchez, Chelsea 's current number one, was beaten at his near post by Josh King's angled shot in the opening Premier League match against Fulham .

He later spilled another effort into a dangerous area, allowing Gonzalo Garcia to score, although Chelsea won 3-2 win at Craven Cottage.

Manager Xavi Alonso initially defended the Spanish goalkeeper after the match and was again asked about him before the Carabao Cup match against Luton Town on Thursday night at Stamford Bridge.

"No, (we have had) normal conversations," he said. "We have talked more about the team thing, about what we did well and what we have to do better.

"It was more about understanding the context. Every game is going to be important because we are in this process that we still need to develop things, we need to make adjustments that are more team-related."

Chelsea 's number two goalkeeper Mike Penders, who returned over the summer from a successful loan spell at Strasbourg, could start instead.

Asked about Penders' involvement, Alonso added: "He's in the squad, so he has an opportunity.

"We will decide and give the team to the players tomorrow, so I prefer to expect that they know first."

articles.title: Gianni Infantino: Uefa set to drop Fifa tournament boycott threat
articles.summary: Uefa is set to drop its threat of boycotting Fifa competitions, having received assurances there will be no repeat of Gianni Infantino's plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors, BBC Sport has been told.
articles.body:
Uefa is set to drop its threat of boycotting Fifa competitions, having received assurances there will be no repeat of Gianni Infantino's plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors, BBC Sport has been told.

The matter will be discussed at a meeting of Uefa's executive committee in Monaco on Thursday.

Earlier this month, European football's governing body said that despite Infantino's plan being aborted following widespread condemnation, the conditions required to prevent a boycott had "not been met".

"Assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again," Uefa insisted.

That came after Infantino had told national member associations that the FFE proposal was "now off the table", and apologised for "errors".

If the boycott threat is lifted, it will mean next month's Under-20 Women's World Cup will proceed as planned.

Six European teams - England, France, Italy, Portugal, Spain and hosts Poland - are scheduled to play in the tournament.

Uefa has led the backlash against Infantino, and along with Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation, is expected to continue to push for an overhaul of Fifa's leadership. Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin has said he expects Infantino to resign or to face a challenge to his role from another candidate at elections in March.

"This isn't a climbdown," said one source close to the discussions, adding that Infantino's opponents "will continue until there are wholesale changes".

"It is not a Uefa defeat, rather the reality of avoiding hurting young players [over a] once-in-a-lifetime opportunity," they added.

"The actions and insistence on change will continue and will win out in the end."

Last month, European football's 55 member associations voted to boycott all Fifa competitions until the Fifa Forward Enterprises proposal was dropped "in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that Fifa will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership".

Fifa and Uefa have been approached for comment.

Culture secretary Lisa Nandy said this month she would not support a boycott of the U20 World Cup.

"I am not generally in favour of sporting boycotts full stop, because I think they divide people from one another. I think they unfairly penalise athletes and competitors who are not responsible for the reason that these boycotts take place," she said.

"What I would like to see actually is football coming together, resolving this, a change of leadership, a change of direction and a very clear message that football belongs to its fans and it will not have women and girls penalised when the women's game is going from strength to strength. And our Lionesses are leading the world in that."

Will a Premier League club break record for transfer sales in one window?

On Tuesday, a group of former players published a statement saying "change is necessary" at the head of Fifa.

Former Manchester United and France defender Mikael Silvestre, who sits on Fifa's Players' Voice Panel, issued a statement on X on Monday in a post he titled "Enough is Enough!".

The statement has been shared on social media by the likes of England defender Lucy Bronze, France's 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit and former England goalkeeper David James.

However on Wednesday, a different group of former players including World Cup-winning Brazil captain Cafu, former Italy striker Christian Vieri, former Portugal captain Pepe and ex-Argentina international Esteban Cambiasso all posted supportive messages for Infantino on social media.

All of the players are so-called Fifa Legends, officially recognised by the governing body.

Vieri's statement said: "Over the past 10 years, we have seen the work Fifa and President Infantino have done to create representativity for players in football, which did not exist.

"We will remain available to support the great evolution our game has seen this past decade, so that it keeps reaching and benefiting people of every country that plays football all around the world."

This news will come as a major relief to the European Women's U20 players that have been in a degree of limbo over recent weeks, but who will now hope they can prepare to travel to Poland to compete in the forthcoming World Cup.

Meanwhile, Fifa president Infantino may well view it as a significant victory in his increasingly acrimonious battle with Uefa, as he seeks to cling to power.

While the nature of the assurances it has received are yet to become clear, despite its tough talk of possible boycotts and legal action, Europe's governing body now runs the risk of being seen to have caved in, having issued what amounted to a hollow threat.

The 33-year-old, who joined from Barnsley in 2019, made a total of 216 appearances for the Bees, scoring 12 times.

Pinnock had been in the final year of his contract with the West London club.

"I'm really excited to join Coventry City and continue my footballing journey with this great club," he said.

"After 25 years, the club are back in the Premier League, and I know how much it must mean to everyone involved. I can't wait to be part of it."

Pinnock played a vital role in Brentford's promotion to the Premier League but has since lost his place in their starting XI, featuring just eight times in all competitions last term.

He joins former team-mate Frank Onyeka in making the switch from Brentford to Coventry this summer.

The Sky Blues have spent over £100m this summer with Pinnock their 10th signing and second defensive reinforcement following the arrival of Aurele Amenda from Eintracht Frankfurt in July.

articles.title: Cardiff City transfer news: Bluebirds closing in on deal to sign Krystian Bielik
articles.summary: Cardiff City are closing in on a deal to sign defender Krystian Bielik from Championship rivals West Bromwich Albion.
articles.body:
Cardiff City are closing in on the signing of centre-half Krystian Bielik from Championship side West Bromwich Albion on a permanent deal.

The 28-year-old made 17 Championship appearances for the Baggies last season as they finished 21st, narrowly avoiding relegation to League One.

The experienced defender - who can also operate as a defensive midfielder - joined Arsenal from Legia Warsaw in 2015 and had spells with Birmingham City, Walsall, Charlton Athletic and Derby County prior to joining West Brom last summer.

Bielik would be Cardiff's fourth senior summer recruit following the arrivals of goalkeeper Nathan Trott, midfielder Jack Moylan and left-back Calum Scanlon, who has returned to the Welsh capital on loan from Liverpool.

Poland international Bielik would be a welcome signing for the Bluebirds, who are currently without a fit central defender in their ranks.

Will Fish, Dylan Lawlor, Calum Chambers and Gabriel Osho are all currently injured, although the latter is thought to be close to a return to action.

The Bluebirds gave a debut to 15-year-old defender Noah Anyadike - who became the youngest player in EFL Cup history - during their 2-1 loss against Norwich City in the second round on Tuesday night.

Bielik could potentially make his Cardiff debut when they host Chris Wilder's Sheffield United on Saturday (15:00 BST).

articles.title: Matt Dibley-Dias: Newport County sign Fulham midfielder on loan
articles.summary: Newport County complete their 11th signing of the summer as midfielder Matt Dibley-Dias arrives on loan from Premier League Fulham.
articles.body:
Newport County have signed Fulham midfielder Matt Dibley-Dias on a short-term loan.

The 22-year-old is reunited with Hayden Mullins, the Exiles head coach who was previously in charge of Fulham's under-21 side.

Dibley-Dias, Newport's 11th signing this summer, made 31 appearances across two seasons under Mullins and was part of the side that lifted the Premier League Cup in 2023-24.

Since joining Fulham at the age of 14, Dibley-Dias has also been named in first-team matchday squads on four occasions for the Cottagers.

The midfielder signed his first professional contract in 2021 and is highly-thought of among Fulham's academy having won Johnny Haynes Academy Player of the Year for the 2022-23 season.

Dibley-Dias spent last season out on loan, featuring five times for League Two side Chesterfield during the first half of the campaign before joining National League outfit Braintree Town, where he made eight appearances - contributing one assist.

He also had a loan spell at Northampton Town in 2024-25.

His arrival provides Mullins with further midfield competition following the summer additions of Harrison Biggins and Kieron Evans.

He will hope to help County build on their positive start to League Two and could make his debut when Mullins' team host Tranmere Rovers at Rodney Parade on Saturday (15:00 BST).

articles.title: Carabao Cup third-round draw: When it is and why certain clubs cannot play each other
articles.summary: The Carabao Cup reaches its third-round stage this week, with the competition’s biggest clubs entering the draw and a host of potentially intriguing ties on...
articles.body:
The Carabao Cup reaches its third-round stage this week, with the competition's biggest clubs entering the draw and a host of potentially intriguing ties on offer.

The draw takes place on Wednesday night, August 26, after the conclusion of Preston North End's second-round meeting with Everton , with the main draw expected at around 10.15pm BST.

A total of 32 teams will make up the third-round draw, including nine Premier League clubs who enter at this stage because of their involvement in European competition.

Arsenal , Manchester City , Manchester United , Liverpool , Aston Villa , Bournemouth , Brighton , Crystal Palace and Sunderland are among those joining the competition at the third-round stage.

That means the draw could immediately produce some fascinating ties between Premier League sides and clubs from the Championship, League One or League Two, while several of England's biggest clubs will be hoping to avoid each other.

There is, however, a significant restriction on the draw. The eight Premier League clubs involved in the Champions League or Europa League cannot face one another in the third round because of fixture congestion and scheduling requirements. A preliminary draw will first determine whether those clubs are at home or away before the main draw takes place.

Brighton, despite their involvement in European competition, are treated differently because their Conference League campaign does not begin until October and they therefore remain part of the main draw.

The Carabao Cup has already produced its share of early drama, with clubs from the Championship and lower divisions looking to make their mark against higher-ranked opposition. With the Premier League's European contingent now entering, the possibility of a major upset increases considerably.

The third-round ties will be played across the weeks commencing September 7 and September 14, with the precise dates and television selections to be confirmed after the draw.

For the Premier League clubs, the competition offers an opportunity to challenge for silverware while also providing valuable minutes for squad players and younger members of their teams.

For the clubs lower down the pyramid, meanwhile, the prospect of welcoming one of the Premier League's biggest names represents both a major sporting occasion and a potentially significant financial boost.

articles.title: Ipswich make superb start with hope of more to come
articles.summary: As first weeks of the season go, Ipswich Town's could not have gone much better.  Gary O'Neil named six debutants in his starting line-up against Sunderland...
articles.body:
As first weeks of the season go, Ipswich Town's could not have gone much better.

Gary O'Neil named six debutants in his starting line-up against Sunderland (seven if you include the returning Julio Enciso ) and one of the big takeaways from the opening-day win was that this did not look like a new team trying to find its feet under a new manager.

A few days later, despite making nine changes, O'Neil's side progressed relatively smoothly into round three of the Carabao Cup at the expense of a Leicester side who finished above them in the Premier League two years ago, and who Town failed to get the better of during six meetings under former boss Kieran McKenna.

Town's rise and Leicester's demise is such that, for the time being, they are rivals no more. Ipswich have left them a long way behind.

In 22-year-old striker Emersonn , Ipswich not only have a first Brazilian to play for the club but they have a rough diamond that has that crucial first goal in his new colours early doors. In the aforementioned Enciso, they may have a player who can potentially win matches from nowhere, as his captain Dara O'Shea has alluded to.

O'Neil has been quick to praise the role that O'Shea and other senior members of the playing squad have played in terms of helping the new faces settle. He has also made it clear that not everything has pleased him since kick-off last Saturday and that there is more to come from his squad. This is an exciting prospect before two mouth-watering fixtures on the immediate horizon.

With Manchester United reeling after an opening-day loss to Hull and Liverpool nowhere near the level Andoni Iraola wants them to be longer term, Ipswich can approach both heavyweights with real hope of adding to their early-season points tally.

articles.title: How many games can Shaw play?
articles.summary: Signing an additional left-back has looked an obvious thing for Manchester United to do.  Luke Shaw started all 38 Premier League games last season and he st...
articles.body:
Signing an additional left-back has looked an obvious thing for Manchester United to do.

Luke Shaw started all 38 Premier League games last season and he started at Hull on Saturday. Of United's past 44 league games, the 31-year-old England international has failed to start just one, the final game of the 2024-25 campaign, four days after the Europa League final defeat by Tottenham - and he went on the post-season tour of Asia immediately afterwards.

Before that, Shaw's injury record had not been great.

Between February 2024 and April 2025, he played as many games for England (three) as he did for his club. He missed three months at the start of the 2023-24 campaign.

There were calf and hamstring issues but also a feeling Erik ten Hag rushed him back too quickly.

More than anyone, Shaw benefited from a 40-game season, allowing him to prepare properly, largely for one game a week, sometimes not even that.

That preparation time will not be repeated.

Although there are blank midweeks between Manchester United's first three games, if they get through two Carabao Cup rounds, they will not have a full midweek without a game, other than during international breaks, until the one that includes Christmas Day.

It is the combination of Shaw's injury record and the crush of games that has led to the feeling another left-back will arrive.

articles.title: Europa League draw: Who is in the draw and who is in each pot?
articles.summary: Our Ask Me Anything team explains who will enter Friday's league phase draw for the 2026-27 Europa League draw
articles.body:
The league phase draw for the 2026-27 Europa League takes place on Friday, 28 August at 12:00 BST in Monaco.

Much like the Champions League draw on Thursday, a total of 36 teams will enter the draw for Europe's second-tier club competition. Just 20 of those teams have been confirmed at present, with the remainder to be made up from the losers of the final round of Champions League qualifying and the winners from the final round of Europa League qualifying.

In the league phase, each team will face eight different teams once, with four home matches and four away matches.

For the draw, the 36 teams will be placed into four pots, with pot one being the highest-ranked and four being the lowest. The pot placements are based on the club's Uefa club coefficient ranking from the five-season period ending at the conclusion of 2025-26.

Each team will face two teams from each of the four pots and cannot face a team from the same country as themselves.

The teams who finish in the top eight will qualify for the Europa League's round of 16. Those between ninth and 24th place will enter the play-off knockout round. The 12 teams ranked between 25th and 36th place will exit the competition when the league phase is concluded.

While the final details of who will qualify are yet to be finalised, the majority of the teams in pot one have been confirmed.

Bayer Leverkusen, Juventus, AC Milan, AZ Alkmaar, Olympiakos, Real Sociedad and Marseille will take seven of the nine pot one places.

The losing team in the Champions League qualifying tie between Fenerbahce and Lyon are guaranteed to enter pot one of the Europa League draw.

As the highest-ranked team still in qualifying, Portuguese outfit Benfica would take the last spot, should they win against Danish side AGF.

Scottish champions Celtic are guaranteed to enter pot two, as are Sparta Prague and Rennes. Belgian side Union Saint-Gilloise will enter either of pot one or two, although two is more likely.

English trio Crystal Palace, Bournemouth and Sunderland will all enter pot two or three, with three being the more likely outcome. Austrian side Sturm Graz will also go in one of those two pots.

Celta Vigo, TSG Hoffenheim, Hapoel Be'er Sheva and NEC Nijmegen will all enter either pot three or four. Torreense, who play their club football in Portugal’s second tier, will also enter either of those pots.

Due to the large number of spots still available, no teams are so far guaranteed to enter pots three or four at present.

articles.title: Ebbsfleet United: Club's future in doubt as National League extend suspension
articles.summary: Ebbsfleet United's suspension from the National League is extended, putting the club's future in serious doubt.
articles.body:
Ebbsfleet United's future is in serious doubt after their suspension from the National League was extended.

Earlier this month, Ebbsfleet's first three National League South games of the season were suspended because of the Kent club's ongoing financial problems.

The National League announced in a statement on Wednesday that a review of the situation by its compliance and licensing committee had found no significant change.

"The club has been given time and opportunity to demonstrate compliance with the league's rules and regulations, but matters cannot continue as has been the case," the statement read.

"The range of actions under rules and regulations include the potential for expulsion from the National League.

"The club is aware that such action is an option, and that it is entirely a matter for the club to satisfy the committee under the rules and regulations, and to remove such as an outcome."

Ebbsfleet remain in debt to HM Revenue and Customs, meaning a winding-up petition remains in place, with doubts therefore remaining over whether they have the financial capacity to complete the season.

The extension of the suspension also means that neither their away match at Farnborough Town on 29 August nor the home game against Horsham two days later will go ahead.

Ebbsfleet have been given until 5pm on 1 September to submit any further information to the National League, who will then carry out a further review.

articles.title: La UEFA pondrá fin al boicot a la FIFA si se cumplen dos condiciones

articles.summary: Considera que tiene garantías de que el plan Infantino no seguirá adelante
articles.body: La UEFA está a punto de retirar su amenaza de boicotear las competiciones de la FIFA, según The Guardian, después de recibir las garantías de que no se repetirá el plan de Gianni Infantino de vender participaciones en la Copa del Mundo a inversores privados. El asunto se discutirá en una reunión del comité ejecutivo de la UEFA este jueves en Mónaco, pero el máximo organismo europeo considera que el escenario ha cambiado tras la marcha atrás de Infantino a su plan inicial. Y pide dos condiciones: que se garantice que el plan no saldrá y que en el futuro tampoco intentará volver a plantearlo. La decisión llega después de que la FIFA retirara a finales de julio el polémico proyecto que provocó el rechazo frontal de las 55 federaciones miembro de la UEFA, las cuales habían pactado el boicot tras revelarse los detalles el mes pasado. El organismo europeo exigía tanto la retirada formal de la propuesta como el compromiso vinculante de no reactivar iniciativas similares a futuro: "No se trata de una derrota de la UEFA, sino de la sensatez de no arruinar una oportunidad única en la vida a los futbolistas jóvenes. Las acciones y la exigencia de reformas continuarán".

articles.title: Julian Alvarez: 'Lies and half-truths' - Atletico Madrid hit back at Barcelona over transfer saga
articles.summary: Barcelona have again restated their desire to sign Julian Alvarez, prompting another angry response from Atletico Madrid.
articles.body:
Atletico Madrid insist there is "0% chance" of selling Julian Alvarez to Barcelona after club president Joan Laporta said they remain interested in signing the forward.

Alvarez has been the subject of intense transfer speculation this summer, and after being booed by Atletico supporters on Sunday during their draw with Villarreal, the 26-year-old missed training on Wednesday.

Reports say Alvarez was unwell, and Atletico have now condemned Laporta's latest video, published on Wednesday, which said Barcelona's €100m (£85.7m) offer remained on the table.

"This is not about money, it's about dignity. The player is being victimised, but the only victim in the Julian case is us," Atletico said.

"They have harmed us economically and socially. There is 0% chance of selling him to Barca.

"There is a campaign of many lies and half-truths. The only one paying for this is Atletico."

In the video, Laporta said the club had great respect for Atletico but the bid they lodged earlier this summer was still on offer.

Sources at Barcelona say they will keep trying to sign Alvarez, who joined Atletico from Manchester City in 2024, until the transfer window ends.

The comments come after weeks of increasingly complicated negotiations and public disagreements between the two clubs.

It also comes as Arsenal continue to show interest in the striker, who is viewed as the Gunners' dream transfer target.

But sources close to the situation say Alvarez still wants to stay in Spain.

Alvarez's Arsenal dilemma amid summer's most bitter transfer tussle

For now, Arsenal are sitting back and watching this unfold, as they become more realistic about their chances of signing Alvarez before next week's transfer deadline.

Alvarez started on the bench on Sunday but was jeered while warming up and there were even louder boos when he came on in the 66th minute.

He headed straight down the tunnel at full-time, rather than joining the rest of the team who were applauding the fans, which drew more boos.

Atleti boss Diego Simeone suggested afterwards that it was a pre-agreed club decision for the forward to head straight to the dressing room.

Speaking before Barcelona's match against Athletic Club on Thursday, head coach Hansi Flick declined to discuss Alvarez directly, saying: "I only want to speak about the situation of the club."

With deadline day approaching on 1 September, the war of words continues and the Argentine World Cup winner's future remains one of the biggest talking points of the transfer window.

Alvarez transfer saga – how did we get here?

The first offer on the table came from Barcelona in May, with reports suggesting the club had opened talks to sign Alvarez.

But in what seems to be a recurrent pattern, Atletico were absolutely adamant that they would not sell Alvarez to Barcelona.

In May, they made a series of social media posts brutally mocking Barca's pursuit of their player to millions of followers, saying they were victims of a "smear campaign".

Alvarez went to the World Cup with Argentina with his future already a major talking point.

Then, in June, in came another big offer from Atleti's city rivals, Real Madrid.

Los Blancos made a €150m (£130m) offer for Alvarez after president Florentino Perez promised supporters that he would make a €150m bid for an unnamed "Galactico" if re-elected.

The offer was rejected by Atletico, with Real Madrid pointing to Alvarez's €500m (£430m) release clause and saying Atletico had "expressed its gratitude for the proposal".

Again, Atleti responded with humorous social media posts, denying any gratitude and remaining adamant that Alvarez would not be sold to Barcelona.

After Argentina's win over Austria in June, Alvarez told media that he had spoken to Atletico and he said that "the best thing for everyone is a transfer", adding: "I want to fulfil my dream".

Those comments effectively confirmed that, despite Atletico's insistence that he was not for sale, the player himself was open to leaving and Barcelona and Paris St-Germain were among the clubs reportedly interested.

Barcelona's interest in Alvarez was driven by their need for a long-term successor to Robert Lewandowski, who left the club this summer.

But Atletico maintained they did not want to sell Alvarez, with chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin saying the club would not sell him "even for 200m euros (£170.8m)".

articles.standfirst: Su clasificación para la fase final de la Conference es importante de cara a la plaza extra de Champions
articles.summary: Su clasificación para la fase final de la Conference es importante de cara a la plaza extra de Champions
articles.body: El Getafe busca finiquitar el pase a la fase liga de Conference League. Y lo hará con una ventaja de la que Bordalás no se fía. Pese al 3-1, el conjunto azulón visita el infierno de Belgrado para verse las caras frente a un Partizán que vive, precisamente, su propia descomposición institucional tras la dimisión de su directiva y de su entrenador, Sasa Ilic, que pese a ello se sentará en el banquillo contra los azulones. El ‘Geta’ no estará solo. El fútbol español estará pendiente de lo que hagan los pupilos de José Bordalás. Su clasificación para el torneo le daría más opciones a LaLiga de luchar la quinta plaza que da acceso a la Champions, algo que este curso ha saboreado el Real Betis gracias a las actuaciones de los españoles en Europa. Viendo los resultado de los equipos de las grandes ligas, el Getafe no puede fallar para evitar que el campeonato español parta ya en desventaja y a remolque. Bordalás llega sin Abqar, sancionado, pero con Mario Martín, ya recuperado y que podría ser de la partida para dar descanso a un medio del campo que no ha parado de jugar en la última semana. Mientras, el Partizan también se agarra a su historia. Tres veces levantó desventajas de al menos dos goles en Europa: ante el Sparta de Praga en la Copa de Europa 1965-66, frente al Queens Park Rangers en la Copa de la UEFA 1984-85 y contra el Sabah en la previa de la Conference 2023-24. Ahora es un rival herido. Después de caer en el Coliseum, el Partizan volvió a perder en la Liga serbia, y quedó antepenúltimo en la tabla con una sola victoria en cinco jornadas. El golpe fue tal que su entrenador, Sasa Ilic, meditó la dimisión. Los dirigentes y la afición consiguieron que continuara, al menos hasta el choque ante el Getafe. Ilic permanecerá en el banquillo con la obligación de salvar algo más que una eliminatoria: el orgullo de un gigante que atraviesa una de sus horas más bajas. Tendrá a casi toda su plantilla disponible. Sólo faltarán Ognjen Ugresic, traspasado este martes al PAOK, e Ibrahim Zubairu, castigado por el club por indisciplina. El técnico confirmó que prescindirá del ghanés por tercer encuentro consecutivo. Por otro lado, el Getafe comunicó que el encuentro será retransmitido a través de su canal de YouTube de forma gratuita.

articles.title: Otra emotiva despedida en La Fábrica: "Ocho temporadas llenas de recuerdos inolvidables"
articles.standfirst: Manu Serrano hace oficial su salida del Madrid para incorporarse al Dépor
articles.summary: Manu Serrano hace oficial su salida del Madrid para incorporarse al Dépor
articles.body: Siguen las despedidas de jugadores de La Fábrica. En esta ocasión, el turno es para Manu Serrano. Tal y como adelantó MARCA ayer, el defensa del Castilla alcanzó un acuerdo para fichar por el Deportivo. Arrancará en su filial, pero con proyección al primer equipo. El canterano, miembro de la histórica generación del triplete del Juvenil A dirigido por Arbeloa en la temporada 22-23 junto a Palacios, Gonzalo, Jacobo Ramón, Manuel Ángel y Nico Paz, entre otros, fue un jugador importante la pasada temporada en el Real Madrid Castilla, lo que tuvo el premio final de su debut en el primer equipo de la mano de Arbeloa. Ahora cierra una etapa de blanco con una emotiva despedida. "Las despedidas nunca son fáciles. Hacerlo de un sitio en donde he sido tan feliz lo hace aún más complicado. Cierro una etapa muy importante en mi vida y de la que me voy muy orgulloso", comienza el mensaje que publicó en sus redes sociales. "Gracias al Real Madrid por apostar por un chico de 14 años y hacerle cumplir todos sus sueños. Debutar con el primer equipo en el Estadio Santiago Bernabéu es uno de los momentos más felices de mi vida y un recuerdo que me llevaré para siempre. Gracias por hacerme sentir lo que es representar al Real Madrid y transmitir sus valores", continúa Manu Serrano. "Estoy muy agradecido a todas las personas de la Ciudad Real Madrid. Grandes profesionales que son la verdadera esencia de la cantera, pero, sobre todo, he compartido momentos inolvidables junto a mis compañeros, personas que me llevo para toda la vida. Ocho temporadas llenas de recuerdos inolvidables, títulos, mucho sacrificio, pero, sobre todo, mucha felicidad. Hasta siempre, Real Madrid", finaliza el defensa, que seguirá su carrera en el Dépor.

articles.title: El Celta ofrece una mejora salarial a Javi Rueda y rechaza la oferta del Nottingham Forest

articles.body: El Celta apuesta por la continuidad de Javi Rueda y así lo demuestra con la importante mejora salarial que este miércoles ha ofrecido al futbolista y rechazando la oferta presentada por el Nottingham Forest. El malagueño amplió su contrato, hasta el año 2029, el pasado 24 de noviembre, y apenas nueve meses después el club vigués le ofrece una mejora de su contrato, convencido de su potencial, valorando su trayectoria y porque se trata de un jugador clave para el entrenador. El lateral, que el pasado sábado disputó media hora en Mestalla, a sus 24 años tiene un excelente futuro por delante. La pasada temporada disputó 2082 minutos, distribuidos en 38 partidos en los que hizo 5 goles y dio 7 asistencias. El Celta con este movimiento reitera su apuesta por su proyecto deportivo, por seguir creciendo y por la valoración de sus futbolistas. Ello no quiere decir que el club ya no tenga que realizar una gran venta en este mercado veraniego, desde principio de temporada se señaló la necesidad del club de cuadrar sus cuentas y que se atenderían ofertas que fuesen irrechazables.

articles.title: Gavi se solidariza con el menor que sufrió la carga policial en el Elche por lucir la estelada
articles.standfirst: A través de las redes sociales
articles.summary: A través de las redes sociales
articles.body: Gavi tiene el corazón azulgrana. Lo dice Hansi Flick, lo dicen sus compañeros, su familia... y sus hechos. El centrocampista andaluz mostró este miércoles su apoyo y su solidaridad con el menor que sufrió la carga policial en Elche por lucir una bandera estelada. A través de las redes sociales, Gavi hizo público su apoyo al joven agredido en las inmediaciones del Martínez Valero el pasado domingo. Lo hizo en un post de la peña de la que forma parte el joven seguidor azulgrana. Precisamente, el Barcelona, que condenó el lunes la agresión policial al menor azulgrana en Elche, decidió hoy no celebrar mañana, antes del encuentro contra el Athletic en el Spotify Camp Nou, el homenaje a los mundialistas, porque considera que no son ni el momento ni el contexto adecuados, y lo sustituyó por una exaltación de la bandera estelada. "Las imágenes son espeluznantes y muy claras. Una vez reconfirmados los hechos, pedimos que se apliquen las sanciones y los castigos pertinentes", comentó hoy Joan Laporta, que fue quien, a través de los medios del club, anunció los cambios reivindicativos. "Que el acto sirva para que los culés y los catalanes podamos ir con la estelada sin que corra peligro nuestra integridad física y que este elemento deje de estar estigmatizado por las fuerzas de seguridad y orden público del Estado", aseveró también el mandatario azulgrana. El Barça repartirá 10.000 enseñas independentistas en el exterior del Spotify Camp Nou.

articles.title: Iván Gil pide paso en la mediapunta
articles.standfirst: El catalán firmó una segunda mitad de mucho nivel el pasado domingo ante el Valladolid
articles.summary: El catalán firmó una segunda mitad de mucho nivel el pasado domingo ante el Valladolid
articles.body: La puesta a punto de Iván Gil en su segunda etapa como armero se cocina a fuego lento. El mediapunta catalán se incorporó a la pretemporada más tarde que sus compañeros, no participó en los dos primeros partidos de pretemporada y tampoco ha formado parte de las alineaciones de Jokin Aranbarri en este arranque de curso. El preparador armero le dio 20 minutos en el debut liguero ante el Tenerife y toda la segunda mitad el pasado domingo frente al Valladolid. A la tercera puede ser la vencida y en el regreso a Andorra, la que fue su casa, podría estrenarse como titular. Sin estar aún a su mejor versión, la aparición del mediapunta tras el descanso fue determinante en la reacción del Eibar ante el Pucela. Aranbarri le situó por detrás de Bautista, escoró a Magunazelaia a la banda derecha y con Aleix lateralizado en los inicios de juego, Gil tuvo libertad para bajar a recibir al centro del campo, lo que generó dudas en la zaga visitante. Todos esos ajustes se hicieron notar en las circulaciones armeras, mucho más fluidas, precisas y verticales. "Llegamos al vestuario y el míster nos dijo cosas que teníamos que corregir. El equipo lo hizo y por eso le dimos la vuelta al partido. Empezamos a generar más, a tener más el balón y a tener nuestra esencia", explica el 21, que va a más con el paso de las sesiones. "Estoy feliz. Me estoy sintiendo muy a gusto tanto con el balón como con los compañeros". Las sensaciones con Aranbarri son inmejorables para un jugador llamado a ser fundamental en la mediapunta. "Es un entrenador que tiene las cosas muy claras. El primer día que llegué me hizo sentir uno más y poco a poco vamos a ir asimilando sus ideas". Gil vivirá una jornada de reencuentros este domingo. "Les guardo un cariño enorme. Estoy feliz de volver allí porque al final te encuentras con gente con la que has conseguido cosas también. Sí que es verdad que tuvimos la época del descenso, pero al final son vivencias a las que guardas un cariño especial por esa gente". A nivel personal, el catalán es consciente de que esta nueva etapa en el Eibar le debe ayudar a recuperar la versión que cautivó a todo Segunda cuando militaba en el Andorra. "Quiero que el Eibar esté en el sitio más arriba posible, competir y ser yo mismo. Llevaba un año y medio ahí en Las Palmas y las cosas no me fueron como me hubieran gustado. Pero al final escojo Eibar porque creo que me puedo reencontrar como jugador, ser feliz y disfrutar".

articles.title: Colorado WR duo earns recognition on Earl Campbell Award watch list
articles.summary: Colorado receivers Joseph Williams and Quentin Gibson earned spots on the Earl Campbell Tyler Rose Award watch list entering the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Colorado wide receiver duo Joseph Williams and Quentin Gibson were named to the Earl Campbell Tyler Rose Award watch list on Tuesday.

The Earl Campbell Tyler Rose Award recognizes the top offensive player from the state of Texas who also exhibits the enduring characteristics that define Earl Campbell: integrity, performance, teamwork, sportsmanship, drive, community and tenacity.

Williams played in 10 games during the 2025 season and finished with 37 receptions for 489 yards and four touchdowns. He nearly won the Earl Campbell Tyler Rose Award Player of the Week during Week 7 against Iowa State, where he hauled in eight receptions for 128 yards and a touchdown.

He enters the 2026 season as one of Colorado 's top four wideouts along with Danny Scudero , DeAndre Moore Jr. and Kam Perry.

Gibson enters his sophomore season after playing in all 12 games as a true freshman. He finished the year with 15 receptions for 71 yards. He made a huge impact on special teams with 25 kickoff returns for 597 yards, an average of 23.9 yards per return. Gibson was tabbed a FWAA Freshman All-American returner for his performance in 2025.

The watchlist will be narrowed to a maximum of 16 semifinalists in November and no more than five finalists in December. The winner will be honored in late January 2027.

articles.summary: La baja de Diego González hace que el valenciano sea una necesidad para el debut del domingo
articles.body: Ya estaba cerrado desde hace unos días y solo faltaba la autorización del Valencia. Tras producirse, Rubén Iranzo viajó a Zaragoza y ya ha firmado su contrato con el conjunto maño que ha hecho oficial su fichaje. El central será zaragocista hasta 2029 y los chés se guardan un porcentaje de una futura venta. El valenciano, que también puede jugar de lateral derecho, se pondrá ya a las órdenes de Ibai Gómez y apunta a ser titular en el debut liguero de los aragoneses este domingo contra el Nástic. La baja de Diego González es por el protocolo de las conmociones y contusiones cerebrales que se produjo en el amistoso frente al filial del Athletic el pasado viernes. Iranzo, de 23 años, formará pareja con Tachi en el centro de la zaga y podrá comenzar a demostrar su valía. En Mestalla llegó a debutar en el primer equipo, tras haberse formado en las categorías inferiores, pero nunca contó con la confianza del club para ganarse un hueco en la plantilla. El defensa, decimocuarto fichaje, no será la última llegada de este mercado. Tras el adiós de Francho Serrano, el club traerá un lateral derecho con Arnau Campeny del Europa como principal candidato. También se firmará a un extremo después de la sorprendente baja de Emil Hansson. No quería apurar hasta el último día, pero a Lalo parece que no le va a quedar otra.

articles.title: 49ers’ Fred Warner says team unbothered by Jed York’s embarrassing arrest
articles.summary: The 49ers aren't talking about Jed York's arrest.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers ' owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend. While you might think a team owner being arrested in a trailer park prostitution bust would be a distraction, the 49ers say it is not. Coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters that since York has been away from training camp, it hasn't really come up.

"From a football standpoint, it has no effect on us," Shanahan said . "As far as what we do day-to-day, what we talk about. It hasn't been mentioned in a meeting today, it doesn't have to do with what happens on the field. Everything outside of there, I think you guys can judge that better than me."

"We're all aware, we all have social media so we see things," Warner said. "But at the same time, I've got a lot of love, a lot of respect for Jed, and don't feel the need to comment on the situation. I think the team was kind of the same way. It really wasn't a conversation being had in the locker room. Of course, yeah, you notice it, but we're so hyper-focused in this building on trying to prepare for Week 1. A lot of guys are on the bubble, trying to make the team. We're just trying to get better as a football team, and letting that personal situation, let it stay personal with him."

It seems unlikely that the players wouldn't have talked about this situation at all, but it makes perfect sense that they're closing ranks around their owner. If it were a player or coach involved in a similar situation, they would probably handle it the same way. The fact that they're addressing it directly and saying they aren't talking about it is likely the best PR strategy available in this situation. And really what affect would this have on the team beyond it being a topic of quiet conversation?

Warner signed a three-year extension with the 49ers ahead of last season.

articles.title: Orta: "Hay jugadores que están negociando sus salidas y se prevén más llegadas"
articles.standfirst: El director deportivo del Valladolid analizó el mercado de fichajes en la presentación de Miguel Rubio y Homam
articles.summary: El director deportivo del Valladolid analizó el mercado de fichajes en la presentación de Miguel Rubio y Homam
articles.body: El director deportivo del Real Valladolid, Víctor Orta, explicó que, en los seis días que restan para que finalice el mercado de fichajes, espera que haya "varias salidas, ya que hay jugadores que están negociándolas, y alguna llegada, ya que se quieren mejorar algunos puestos". Tras la presentación de Homam y Miguel Rubio, los dos últimos refuerzos del club blanquivioleta, Orta advirtió de que en esta recta final, "todo se acelera y se abren muchas puertas, por lo que hay que estar atentos a todo, siempre que sean jugadores que se puedan pagar y tener, y que sumen". En esa lista de salidas se encuentran Stanko Juric, Marcos André y Vegard Erlien, todos ellos con fichas altas, por lo que tendría un claro beneficio en el límite salarial de la plantilla blanquivioleta, si estos lograran encontrar acomodo en otro club. Además, el Valladolid quiere reforzar algunas posiciones, como la de portero, pero lo que surja "se valorará detenidamente, porque es importante acertar" y, en este sentido, destacó la inyección de 14 millones hecha por la propiedad del club, encabezada por Gabriel Solares, que ha permitido inscribir a los jugadores. "En este club nunca ha hecho nadie una inversión tan grande, con un riesgo personal, a través de un crédito participativo que supone un 25 por ciento de implementación en plantilla, y que ha dado soporte a la dirección deportiva, llegando, además, en un tiempo récord", precisó. Y advirtió de que la responsabilidad, ahora, es suya, de ahí que vaya a estudiar todo detenidamente hasta el último día de mercado, si bien tiene claro que "se ha mejorado la plantilla, la calidad y el nivel de fútbol con las nuevas llegadas, y solo hay que tratar de que todas las piezas se ajusten". En este sentido, admitió que no está contento con las dos derrotas que ha sufrido el equipo en el inicio de liga, pero considera que "sobre 200 minutos, se ha sido superior a los rivales durante 120 o 130 y sólo ha faltado esa efectividad que los otros sí han tenido". "Quizá ha faltado un poco de agresividad ofensiva y definición, pero esto también tiene que ver con el proceso, ya que los jugadores se siguen conociendo y tienen que buscar conexiones para ser peligrosos arriba. Las sensaciones no han sido malas, aunque sí el resultado, y prefiero quedarme con lo bueno", concluyó.
